questions.question: Which condition, also known as icterus, causes a yellowing of your skin and the whites of your eyes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** jaundice**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jaundice (Icterus)** is a condition where the skin, the whites of the eyes (sclera), and sometimes other tissues develop a yellow tint.
 
• This yellowing happens because of an excessive buildup of a substance called **bilirubin** in the blood.
 
• Bilirubin is a yellow pigment produced during the normal breakdown of red blood cells.
 
• Normally, the liver processes bilirubin and excretes it into bile, which helps digest fats.
 
• The bile is then eliminated from the body through stool.
 
• Causes of Jaundice
 
 
• Pre-hepatic (before the liver):
 
• Caused by increased destruction of red blood cells (hemolysis).
 
• Examples: Sickle cell anaemia, malaria.
 
• Hepatic (in the liver):
 
• Caused by liver diseases that impair its ability to process bilirubin.
 
• Examples: Hepatitis, cirrhosis, alcoholic liver disease.
 
• Post-hepatic (after the liver):
 
• Caused by an obstruction in bile ducts that prevents bilirubin from being excreted.
 
• Examples: Gallstones, tumors, bile duct strictures.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Ichthyosis**

 
 
• Ichthyosis refers to a group of skin disorders that cause dry, scaly, and thickened skin, resembling fish scales.
 
 
• It is a chronic condition, often genetic, though it can sometimes occur due to other health issues (acquired ichthyosis).
 
 
 
 
 
• Eczema
 
 
• Eczema (also known as atopic dermatitis) is a chronic inflammatory skin condition that causes red, itchy, and inflamed patches on the skin.
 
 
• It’s commonly triggered by allergens, irritants, or stress.
 
 
 
 
 
• Pemphigus
 
 
• Pemphigus is a rare autoimmune disorder that causes painful blisters on the skin and mucous membranes (such as the mouth, throat, and genitals).
 
• The body’s immune system mistakenly attacks the proteins that hold skin cells together.

questions.question: What is the relationship between interest rate and demand for money?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Inverse**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Interest rates bear an inverse relationship with the demand for money.
 
• Opportunity costs of holding money will be high when interest rates are high;
 
 
• people are losing out on possible earnings that interest-bearing investments could have generated.
 
• When interest rates are high, the opportunity cost of holding money increases because people can earn more by investing their money rather than keeping it as cash.
 
• This leads to a **lower demand for money** for transactional and speculative purposes
 
 
 
• When interest rates are low, the opportunity cost of holding money is low.
 
• People prefer holding more money for transactions or precautionary needs because the benefit of investing it is minimal.
 
• This leads to a higher demand for money.
 
• The relationship can be visualized using the liquidity preference theory by John Maynard Keynes:
 
• The demand for money (liquidity preference) decreases as the interest rate increases, and vice versa.

questions.question: When electricity is passed through water, what kind of chemical reaction occurs?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Decomposition**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When electricity is passed through water, a **decomposition reaction** occurs, specifically **electrolysis of water**.
 
• What happens during electrolysis?
 
• Water ( H2OH_2O H2​O) breaks down into its component gases:2H 2 ​ O(l) Electricity ​ 2H 2 ​ (g)+O 2 ​ (g)
 
• Hydrogen gas is released at the **cathode** (negative electrode).
 
• Oxygen gas is released at the **anode** (positive electrode).
 
• Why is this a decomposition reaction?
 
 
• In a decomposition reaction, a single compound splits into two or more simpler substances.
 
• Here, water splits into hydrogen and oxygen, making it a decomposition reaction.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Displacement:
 
 
• In a displacement reaction, one element displaces another in a compound. 
 
 
 
• Double displacement:
 
 
• This involves the exchange of ions between two compounds. 
 
 
 
• Combination:
 
 
• In a combination reaction, two or more substances combine to form a single compound, which is the opposite of what happens here.

questions.question: Which of the following can be represented as a functional unit of nature?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ecosystem**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• An **ecosystem** is a functional unit of nature because it represents a system where living organisms (plants, animals, microorganisms) interact with one another and with their non-living environment (soil, water, air, sunlight) in a self-sustaining manner.
 
• Characteristics of an Ecosystem:
 
 
• Biotic Components: Living organisms such as plants, animals, and microbes.
 
• Abiotic Components: Non-living factors like sunlight, water, air, and soil.
 
• Interactions: These components interact through processes like energy flow (food chains) and nutrient cycling, making it functional.

questions.question: Which of the following statements correctly defines the green revolution?

options.text: It is a new strategy in agriculture to produce food grains, especially wheat and rice.
It is a new strategy to increase the share of the forest.
It is a new strategy to use green colour for all purposes.
It is a new strategy to use only herbal products.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__It is a new strategy in agriculture to produce food grains, especially wheat and rice__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **Green Revolution refers to a significant transformation in agriculture that began in the 1940s and 1950s,**

 
 
• aimed at increasing food production, particularly in developing countries, **by using new agricultural technologies and practices.**
 
• **So this statement is correct**
 
 
 
• **Green Revolution**:
 
 
• **High-yielding varieties (HYVs) of seeds,** especially for crops like wheat and rice, were developed and promoted.
 
• **Increased use of chemical fertilizers and pesticides** to improve crop yields.
 
• **Mechanization of farming **through the use of modern equipment like tractors, harvesters, etc.
 
• **Irrigation systems were improved **to ensure a more reliable water supply to crops.
 
 
 
• The **Green Revolution led to a significant increase in food production, particularly in countries like India**, helping to prevent famines and making countries self-sufficient in staple crops like rice and wheat.

questions.question: At what latitude does the easterly jet stream blow over peninsular India during the summer months?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**14o**N__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The easterly jet stream over Peninsular India during the summer months typically blows around the 14°N latitude.
 
• This jet stream, known as the Tropical Easterly Jet (TEJ), is a low-level jet stream that flows from the east to west during the summer and plays an important role in the monsoon dynamics.
 
• The easterly jet stream is located at an altitude of around 10 km above the surface, and it is stronger during the summer months when the monsoon winds are active.
 
• The jet stream is found mainly over Peninsular India and parts of the Bay of Bengal at around 14°N latitude.
 
• The position of the easterly jet can influence the intensity and onset of the Indian summer monsoon.

questions.question: Which of the following celebrations is dedicated to Sun God and his wife Usha to thank them for sustaining life on earth and for granting wishes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Chhath Puja__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Chhath is predominantly a Hindu festival dedicated to the Sun god and his wife Usha with the motive of thanking them for providing the bounties of life on the Earth.
 
• The literal meaning of the word chhath is sixth and hence, this festival is celebrated on the sixth day of the Kartika month of the Hindu calendar "Vikram Samvat".
 
• The festival has a duration of four days. The rituals under this festival include a holy bath, keeping the fast, remaining in water for long periods of time, along with offering prayers and food to the setting sun and the rising sun.
 
• The main worshipers are known as Parvaitin,(usually women). Although, it's seen that sometimes men also observe this festival as it is essentially not a gender-specific festival.
 
• The festival is observed primarily in Mithila Province of Nepal, Terai-Madhesh region of Nepal along with the Indian states of Bihar, Jharkhand, and UP.
 
• Moreover, it is also observed in areas where migrants from the above-mentioned areas have their presence. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Madai Festival**

 
 
• The Madai Festival is celebrated primarily by the Gond tribes of Madhya Pradesh and is a significant cultural event that showcases their rich traditions and heritage.
 
• It typically involves vibrant rituals, traditional dance forms, music, and communal feasting, reflecting the community's connection to nature and agriculture.
 
• The festival usually marks the harvesting season and is a time for the tribes to give thanks for the bounty received.
 
 
 
• **Vishwakarma Puja**
 
 
• Vishwakarma Puja is dedicated to Lord Vishwakarma, the divine architect and craftsman of the universe, celebrated by artisans, builders, and craftsmen across India.
 
• This festival often includes the worship of tools, machinery, and vehicles, symbolizing the reverence for craftsmanship and engineering skills.
 
• The Puja is marked by colorful decorations, offerings, and cultural performances, emphasizing creativity and innovation in various trades.
 
 
 
• **Sorath Sabha**
 
 
• Sorath Sabha refers to a cultural and social gathering primarily associated with the Rajput community, particularly in the Sorath region of Gujarat.
 
• These gatherings promote community bonding, sharing of cultural traditions, and discussions on social issues, fostering a sense of unity among members.
 
• The Sabha often features traditional music, dance, and storytelling, highlighting the rich history and heritage of the Rajput community.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution explains that the executive power of every state shall be so exercised as not to impede or prejudice the exercise of the executive power of the Union, and the executive power of the union shall extend to the giving of such directions to a state as may appear to the Government of India to be necessary for that purpose?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Article 257**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 257 of the Constitution of India explains that the executive power** of every state shall be exercised in a way that does not impede or prejudice the exercise of the executive power of the Union
 
• **Article 257(1) of the Constitution of India states that the executive power of every state shall be exercised in a way that does not impede or prejudice the exercise of the executive power of the Union. **
 
• **This article is essential to ensure that the Union and the states exercise their executive power **in a harmonious manner.
 
• It **also enforces the principle of Union supremacy** by giving appropriate directions in the event of irreconcilable differences on vital issues. 
 
• Article 257 shapes the relationship between the center and states in India, addressing the principle of federalism

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Article 261 (Public acts, records, and judicial proceedings)
 
 
• It ensures that full faith and credit shall be given throughout the territory of India to public acts, records, and judicial proceedings of the Union and states.

 Judicial Process:
 
• The law defines how acts, records, and judgments will be authenticated and proved for recognition across state borders.
 
 
 
• Article 247 (Power of Parliament to provide for the establishment of certain additional courts)
 
 
• It grants the Parliament the authority to establish additional courts for better administration of laws made by it regarding matters listed in the Union List.
 
• This article is used to ensure the efficient handling of cases related to Union List subjects, allowing the central government to extend judicial infrastructure.
 
 
 
• Article 123 (Power of the President to promulgate Ordinances during recess of Parliament)
 
 
• It allows the President to issue ordinances when Parliament is not in session, and immediate action is needed, with the same effect as a law passed by Parliament.
 
• These ordinances must be approved by Parliament within six weeks of reassembling, or they cease to operate.

questions.question: In 2021, in which of the following states did the Prime Minister lay the foundation stone for the Raja Mahendra Pratap Singh State University?

questions.question: In the year 1952, who among the following lent his voice for the film 'Amar Bhupali', which was being produced in two languages simultaneously and he sang in both Bengali and Marathi?

__

• He is renowned for his versatile singing in various Indian languages, and for this film, he sang in both **Bengali** and **Marathi**, as it was produced in two languages simultaneously.
 
• Manna Dey had an incredibly diverse repertoire that included classical, semi-classical, folk, and contemporary songs

• such as **S.D. Burman**, **R.D. Burman**, and **Salil Chowdhury**. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **He is known for his distinctive voice and expressive singing style. Hits like "Mere Sapno Ki Rani," "Ek Ladki Bheegi Bhaagi Si," and "Khaike Paan Banaras Wala**" are some of his timeless classics that showcase his versatility and creativity.
 
 
 
• ** Hemanta Mukherjee**
 
 
• Hemanta Mukherjee was a **prominent playback singer **in Indian cinema, especially known for his work in Bengali films.
 
• His** contributions to Hindi music were also significant, with many memorable songs in the 1950s and 60s.**
 
• His rich and soulful voice earned him a place among the greats.
 
• Songs like **"Tumi Robe Nirobe" and "Bajlo Tomar Alor Benu"** highlight his mastery in conveying deep emotions through music.
 
 
 
• ** Debabrata Biswas**
 
 
• **Folk and Ghazal Singer**: Debabrata Biswas was celebrated for his renditions of Bengali folk songs and ghazals.
 
• He was **known for preserving traditional music while also introducing innovative elements.**
 
• He contributed significantly to Bengali culture and music through his performances and recordings, promoting folk traditions and winning the hearts of many with his emotive singing style.

questions.question: When was the High Court and Supreme Court Judges (Salaries and Conditions of Service) Amendment Bill, 2021 introduced in Lok Sabha?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**30 November 2021.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The High Court and Supreme Court Judges (Salaries and Conditions of Service) Amendment Bill, 2021** was introduced in Lok Sabha on **30 November 2021.**

 
 
• The bill seeks to amend the salaries and conditions of service for the judges of the High Court and the Supreme Court of India.
 
• It aims to streamline and update provisions to reflect contemporary requirements and standards for the judiciary.
 
• The introduction of the bill is part of ongoing efforts to ensure the independence and efficiency of the judicial system in India.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Indian judiciary** is an independent body, separate from the executive and legislative branches of the government.
 
• The **Supreme Court** is the highest judicial forum and final court of appeal under the Constitution of India.
 
• The **High Courts** operate at the state level and are below the Supreme Court in the judicial hierarchy.
 
• The **terms and conditions** of service for judges are critical to maintaining judicial independence and integrity.
 
• Periodic amendments ensure that the judiciary is equipped to meet modern challenges and uphold the rule of law.
